science.title: Fossil shark teeth record a microscale pathway for ferromanganese oxide nucleation and Li-Ni enrichment in deep-sea biogenic substrates
science.description: Marine ferromanganese crusts and nodules are major reservoirs of critical metals considered essential for a low-carbon economy, yet the mechanisms governing their initial formation remain poorly documented. Here, we integrate Micro-CT, SEM-EDS, EPMA, LA-ICP-MS, TEM, Raman spectroscopy, and XANES to reconstruct the initial stages of Fe–Mn oxide (FMO) formation in fossil shark teeth from the Rio Grande Rise (southwestern Atlantic Ocean). We document a four-stage FMO mineralization sequence preserved within dentin tubules: (1) bioapatite alteration and organic matter degradation, potentially associated with endolithic bioerosion; (2) precipitation of nanoscale goethite onto dentin tubule walls, associated with phosphate release and pH buffering; (3) Mn oxidation and precipitation of lithiophorite, a layered Mn(III–IV) oxide enriched in Li (~ 650 µg g–1) and Ni (~ 37,000 µg g–1) overgrowing goethite, with lithiophorite-bearing domains characterized by a high average Mn oxidation state of ~ 3.6; and (4) selective redistribution of REY into altered bioapatite, while Ce remains preferentially associated with FMO, followed by late clay-rich infilling. These results highlight the importance of biogenic substrates and confined dentin microenvironments in early FMO nucleation and phase-specific metal redistribution and retention, providing a microscale model for metal partitioning during the initial stages of deep-sea FMO mineralization.

science.title: Prognostic significance and clinicopathologic prediction of tumor deposits in non-metastatic colon mucinous adenocarcinoma
science.description: Colon mucinous adenocarcinoma (CMAC) is a prognostically unfavorable subtype in which tumor deposits (TDs) are an under-recognized adverse feature with uncertain prognostic relevance and a risk of under-detection. From the SEER database we assembled 1372 non‑metastatic CMAC patients (7:3 training/internal‑validation split) plus an external cohort of 398 patients from the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University, using Kaplan–Meier analysis, multivariable Cox regression, and logistic regression to characterize TD prognosis and to develop a model predicting TD presence. TDs were independently associated with poorer cancer-specific survival after adjustment for positive lymph node (PN) burden; no statistically significant TD × PN interaction was detected (P > 0.05), although the PN = 0 subgroup estimate was imprecise and not statistically significant. A nomogram using six routine clinicopathologic predictors—tumor size, site, grade, invasion depth, PN count, and perineural invasion—predicted TD presence with good discrimination (AUC = 0.820, 0.768, 0.784 for training, internal‑validation, and external cohorts), good calibration (Brier 0.095, 0.098, 0.086), and positive net benefit at 5–25% threshold probabilities. Collectively, TDs provide adverse prognostic information after accounting for nodal burden in CMAC, and the nomogram, externally validated only for TD prediction, estimates the probability of recorded TD positivity and may help identify cases warranting additional pathological attention; the survival findings require further validation in multicenter studies.

science.title: Prioritizing heat stress indices for cognitive performance assessment using a Fuzzy Delphi-FAHP framework
science.description: Occupational heat exposure induces physiological strain and can impair cognitive performance, exacerbating occupational error and accident risks. Although numerous heat stress indices exist, their theoretical and practical suitability for cognitive-related assessments remains ambiguous. This study established a structured multicriteria decision-making framework integrating the Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM) and Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) to prioritize candidate heat stress indices for occupational cognitive risk evaluation. Candidate indices and screening criteria identified via literature review and expert consensus ($$n=25$$) were evaluated using FDM, followed by FAHP with Chang’s extent analysis to derive criteria weights and overall index priorities. A one-at-a-time $$+10\%$$ sensitivity analysis was performed to verify model stability. Following FDM screening, six criteria and seven indices were retained. Predictive capability for cognitive performance (weight: 0.265), physiological relevance (0.229), and reliability/reproducibility (0.177) emerged as the most critical evaluation criteria. Among evaluated indices, the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI, priority: 0.214) ranked highest, followed by Predicted Heat Strain (PHS, 0.201) and Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT, 0.168), whereas traditional empirical indices demonstrated lower suitability. Sensitivity analysis confirmed exceptional rank stability (Spearman’s $$\rho\:=0.964-1.000$$). Overall, comprehensive, physiologically grounded thermal indices provide superior suitability for cognitive-related heat stress assessment over simple empirical metrics. The proposed framework delivers a transparent, robust decision-support tool for occupational safety and health practitioners.

science.title: Risk assessment of insulator contamination in thermal power plants by integrating dynamic physical priors and spatiotemporal heterogeneous graphs
science.description: To address the problem of predicting insulator fouling risks at thermal power plants resulting from the combined effects of various source-side facilities and meteorological conditions, we propose the Causal-STHGN model. This spatiotemporal heterogeneous graph model integrates dynamic physical priors. This paper first constructs a semantic graph of power plant entities. Source-side facility nodes are mapped to insulator monitoring points as heterogeneous nodes. Then, by integrating spatial geometric relationships, wind field directionality, source-side state characteristics, and moisture condition modulation, the model calculates dynamic physical causal priors and edge-weight priors. Furthermore, it constrains spatial dependency learning through a prior-bias graph attention mechanism. A parallel temporal structure is employed to jointly model short-term disturbances and long-term evolutionary trends. Finally, leakage current is used as a supervised proxy to calibrate the continuous risk representation, thereby evaluating the model’s ability to characterize key processes such as moisture-induced excitation and rain scouring. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method demonstrates strong overall performance across metrics including overall prediction accuracy, risk alerts, and physical consistency, and exhibits risk responses that are more in line with reality within typical event windows.

science.title: Locusts get a sensory assist from nanomaterials
science.description: Scientists have long explored the idea of using insects as our agents in the field in places where humans won’t fit or survive. Imagine a cockroach in an earthquake zone, able to skitter into the rubble to map out exactly where human chemical signatures can be found; or a grasshopper leaping through a minefield to bring back a map of the bombs based on the vapors it encountered. Recent research from Washington University in St. Louis brings this sci-fi concept one step closer to reality.
